name: Lip filler

card.summary: Injected gel that adds lip volume and definition; well documented in trials, temporary, and a minor lever in forum rating systems that put more weight on mouth width.
card.note: Swelling and bruising are common; vascular complications are rare but serious, and results fade as the filler is absorbed.

quick.overview:
Lip filler is the injection of a gel, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), into the lips to add volume, define the border or improve proportions. It is one of the most widely performed non-surgical cosmetic treatments, and multiple randomized trials have compared HA lip products.

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a cheap, low-commitment tweak for thin lips, though some posters argue that mouth width matters more than fullness and that filler cannot widen the mouth.
quick.mechanism: HA gels bind water and add volume where injected, and reviews call HA the gold standard lip filler because it is biocompatible and reversible [2]. Other methods include fat transfer, collagen and permanent fillers, with different durations [17].
quick.risks: Swelling and bruising commonly last up to a week [17]. Reviewers of lip safety describe complications that can be severe, note that complications are underreported, and say prospective randomized trials on the safety literature are lacking [4]. Overfilling can look unnatural [17].

lead: Lip filler, or lip augmentation with fillers, is the injection of a soft-tissue filler, most commonly a hyaluronic acid (HA) gel, to increase lip volume, enhance the vermilion border or improve the ratio between the upper and lower lip [1][5]. Perioral tissues are among the first to show ageing, and reviews say many patients seek perioral fillers as their first cosmetic treatment [3].

Reviews describe HA fillers as the gold standard for lip augmentation because they are biocompatible and reversible [2]. Randomized, multicenter trials have compared HA gels with each other, including a head-to-head comparison of four products [6][7]. Fat transfer and surgical approaches such as the lip lift are alternative methods [9][11].

A review of lip-filler safety states that the results are impressive but so are the reported complications, that there is a paucity of prospective randomized trials on safety, and that complications are under-reported [4]. In looksmaxxing communities lip filler is discussed as a small, accessible modification, alongside views that proportions of mouth to nose matter more than lip volume [16].
infobox: Injectable soft-tissue filler, usually hyaluronic acid [2]
Varies by product; Restylane about six months, some HA claims up to 1 to 1.5 years [17]
Fat transfer, lip lift, other fillers [9][11][17]

paras: Reviews describe lip anatomy in layers of skin, muscle and mucosa, with age-related volume loss, thinning of the vermilion border and flattening of the philtrum, and say treatment should be tailored to the individual, including ethnic differences in lip structure and cultural preferences [2]. Injection techniques include needles and cannulas, with attention to the vascular supply of the lips [2][1]. Perioral fillers can also be applied to the philtral columns, oral commissures and surrounding folds [3].

According to Wikipedia, surgeons tried injecting paraffin into the lips around 1900 without success, liquid silicone was used from the early 1960s and abandoned about thirty years later over safety and appearance concerns, injectable bovine collagen became the standard around 1980, and newer products appeared after 2000 [17]. The shift since then has been toward HA fillers such as Restylane and Juvederm [17].

A 14-year analysis of procedure statistics from the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery covers trends in nonsurgical aesthetic procedures including fillers [12]. Trials of HA lip fillers typically assess lip fullness scales over months: a multicenter randomized double-blind study of 158 patients with thin lips compared a novel HA gel with a commercial comparator over six months [7], a non-inferiority randomized study tested a lidocaine-containing product [8], and an open-label randomized postmarket study followed another lidocaine product for short- and long-term safety [10]. The duration of results depends on the product, with HA fillers lasting roughly six months or longer according to Wikipedia [17].

Wikipedia lists redness, swelling and itching as common reactions and says swelling and bruising can last up to a week; other complications include bleeding, lumps, uneven lips and overfilling that appears unnatural [17]. Reviews of HA lip injections state that complications can be severe, and the authors emphasise anatomy knowledge and small aliquots of product to lower risk [4]. Across fillers, blindness from retrograde embolization is described as rare but usually permanent [18].

Human studies include randomized, multicenter trials comparing HA lip fillers with each other [6][7][8][10], a randomized trial comparing two upper lip augmentation approaches (V-Y technique versus micro-fat injection) on patient satisfaction [9], and reviews of technique and safety [1][4]. Registered trials include studies of four HA fillers [13], a new lip filler [14] and HA filler in ethnic lip augmentation [15].

On looksmax.org, one thread asks how common lip-filler complications are and whether an allergy test exists, with the poster saying thin lips are a major perceived flaw; replies range from the view that fillers are 'cope' because mouth width relative to nose width matters, to advice to see a plastic surgeon and that the amount used is small and cheap [16].

timeline.event: Paraffin injected into lips by surgeons, without success [17]
Liquid silicone enters use, later abandoned over health and appearance concerns [17]
Injectable bovine collagen becomes the benchmark filler [17]
HA fillers such as Restylane and Juvederm become widely used [17]

lore.intro: Lip filler is treated as an accessible way to address thin lips, but forum users dispute how much it matters relative to facial proportions [16].

claims.claim: Fuller lips are a cheap, easy improvement.
claims.believers: A poster says thin lips are a major perceived flaw and that fixing them could raise perceived attractiveness, while another says the filler quantity is small so the cost is low [16].
claims.experts: Reviews report that HA fillers are temporary and reversible and widely used [2]; trials measure lip fullness scales rather than rated attractiveness [7].

claims.claim: Lip filler is cope; mouth width relative to nose width matters more.
claims.believers: A reply states that mouth width relative to nose width matters more than lip fullness [16].
claims.experts: No published study in the sources examines mouth-to-nose ratio versus lip volume; lip anatomy reviews emphasise tailoring to ethnicity and proportions [2].
